title: Check: Effect of Surface Area on Rate

questions.stem: Why does powdered calcium carbonate react faster with hydrochloric acid than marble chips of the same mass?

options.text: Because the powder contains more calcium carbonate
Because the powder has a much larger surface area, exposing more particles to react
Because the powder is at a higher temperature
Because the powder changes the concentration of the acid

questions.explanation: Powdered calcium carbonate has a much larger total surface area than marble chips of the same mass. More particles on the surface are exposed to and can collide with the acid particles. This leads to more collisions per second and therefore a faster rate of reaction.

questions.stem: When investigating the effect of surface area, why is it important to use the same mass of solid in each experiment?

options.text: To ensure the solid dissolves at the same rate
To keep the amount of reactant constant, so only surface area is changed
To make the experiment look more professional
To ensure the same volume of gas is collected each time

questions.explanation: Using the same mass ensures it is a fair test where surface area is the only variable changed. If different masses were used, the total amount of reactant would vary, affecting both the rate and the total amount of product. The same mass also ensures the same final volume of gas is produced.
